about: The narration of the lab-comparison chapter and the takeaway of the two-year cut (twin/video/figs5_labs.py; Kokoro v1.0, af_heart, through twin/video/narration.py's machinery). One entry per line, in order: id; seg (labs or takeaway); part (the card that starts with this line); gap (seconds of silence before it, after the line before); text. A line is placed by figs5_labs.layout() from the recorded lengths, so nothing is timed by hand and a re-render after a change of round keeps the cards in step. Every number is a placeholder: {path:format} reads out/twin<R>/video/numbers.json (numbers5.numbers()); path*K and path/K scale it; {path~span} says a {lo, hi} span as '1.3 to 1.4' or, when both ends print the same, '1.3' (~span0 for whole numbers). No figure is typed in: figs5_labs.check_numbers() fails on any digit outside a placeholder. claims lists the worded statements the line makes (numbers5.claims_by_key()); when one fails, the first alt whose `unless` claims all fail and whose own claims hold is spoken instead, and if none fits the check stops and names the line. src says what on screen the line reads.

lines.text: Now the two labs, like for like: the same policy and the same stock rule in both, over {labs.n_seeds:d} seeds each. All of it is simulated.
lines.src: the card's caption and legend: the same policy and stock rule in both labs, 16 seeds per arm, simulated

lines.text: Aluminium's first target, the best existing alloy, is a tie with the heuristic. With BOFN or pKGFN in both labs it comes {labs.sum.al_T1_opt.af.lo:.1f} times sooner, and every interval includes one.
lines.src: the aluminium panel's first block: tables.md section 1, Aluminium T1, heuristic, BOFN and pKGFN, both ordering as they go and both stocked

lines.text: Aluminium's halfway target comes {labs.sum.al_T2_opt.af~span} times sooner with an optimizer in both labs. With the heuristic, about half the seeds get there in either lab.
lines.src: the aluminium panel's second block: tables.md section 1, Aluminium T2

lines.text: Copper is where the automated lab leads: {labs.sum.cu_funnel.af~span} times sooner with the funnel, and at least {labs.sum.cu_opt.af~span} times with BOFN or pKGFN.
lines.src: the copper panel: tables.md section 1, Copper T1 and T2

lines.text: Where the automated lab does not win. Aluminium's first target is a tie: with the heuristic, the automated lab prints most of its first alloys at the same partners, before its own printer comes online around day {nowin.online.midi:.0f}.
lines.src: tile 1: the tie's factors, where each seed's first alloy past the target was printed, and the in-house MIDI's median day online (like5.json used.online_median_d)

lines.text: The optimizers reach that first target later than the heuristic: in the stocked automated lab, on day {labs.arms.vertical|bofn3|reorder.flaime_al.T1.day:.0f} with BOFN, against day {labs.arms.vertical|fast|reorder.flaime_al.T1.day:.0f}.
lines.src: tile 2: each arm's median day to aluminium's best existing alloy (tables.md, The arms)

lines.text: A stocked conventional lab keeps up with an automated lab that orders its metal as it goes: {nowin.rev.al_T1~span} times on aluminium's first target.
lines.src: tile 3: tables.md section 1, Aluminium T1, the column 'vertical lean, conventional stocked'

lines.text: And reaching a target costs the campaigns no less: about the same money with both labs stocked, and more with an optimizer when both order as they go.
lines.src: tile 4: tables.md section 1, cost on one basis (campaign spend to the target)

lines.text: Where it does win: copper, with every policy and in every pairing, mostly through its own DED machine, in house from around day {nowin.online.mxlab:.0f}. And aluminium's halfway target, when both labs run an optimizer.
lines.src: the card 'Where it does win': copper's factors and seeds, where each first alloy past the target was deposited, the in-house MX-Lab's median day online, aluminium's halfway target

lines.text: Money, as spending over time. With all of it available on day zero, the automated lab has spent {money.share_pct:.0f} percent of aluminium's two-year money by day {money.d90.auto.flaime_al.day:.0f}, and of copper's by day {money.d90.auto.onr_cu.day:.0f}. Then it idles.

alt.text: Money, as spending over time. With no limit on it, the automated lab had spent {money.end.auto.flaime_al.median/1000:.0f} thousand dollars on aluminium by the end of the two years, and {money.end.auto.onr_cu.median/1000:.0f} thousand on copper.

lines.src: the two spend plots: the automated lab's median curve and its 90 % mark (like5.json arms.<arm>.money, tables.md The arms)

lines.text: The conventional lab, with the same policy, spreads its spending over both years: by the end it has spent {money.end.conv.flaime_al.share*100:.0f} percent of aluminium's money and {money.end.conv.onr_cu.share*100:.0f} percent of copper's.

alt.text: The conventional lab, with the same policy, had spent {money.end.conv.flaime_al.median/1000:.0f} thousand dollars on aluminium and {money.end.conv.onr_cu.median/1000:.0f} thousand on copper.

lines.src: the two spend plots: the conventional lab's dashed median curve and its end label (the rows' spend_curve)

lines.text: Counting fixed costs, an aluminium alloy costs about {econ.arms.vertical|bofn3|reorder.flaime_al.per_alloy/1000:.0f} thousand dollars with BOFN in the automated lab, against {econ.arms.conventional|bofn3|reorder.flaime_al.per_alloy/1000:.0f} thousand in the conventional lab.
lines.src: the cost table: tables.md section 3, per alloy (with fixed), BOFN, stocked, aluminium

lines.text: So, in this simulated benchmark, like for like. Copper comes sooner in the automated lab with every policy: {labs.sum.cu_funnel.af~span} times with the funnel, and at least {labs.sum.cu_opt.af.lo:.1f} times with an optimizer.
Aluminium's first target is a tie. Its halfway target comes {labs.sum.al_T2_opt.af~span} times sooner, and only with an optimizer in both labs. There, the policy does more than the lab.
And the automated lab is not cheaper. Its two-year money is spent in about {take.months~span0} months, and with fixed costs each aluminium alloy costs about twice as much.
